title: Dedicated burst: add priority tiers (gold/silver/standard) with anti-starvation constraints
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Context: Dedicated burst pools are shared across multiple tenants (within a region/hardware class). We already enforce per-tenant burst caps + cooldowns + a pool-level safety cap, but we need an explicit tiering model for Enterprise accounts (e.g., Gold/Silver) so we can preferentially admit burst while still protecting baseline tenants and preventing starvation.

This PR adds Priority Tiers to the burst admission controller fairness layer. The tier affects the tenant’s effective burst token refill rate / weight when the shared pool is contended.

Key points:
- Adds `priority_tier` to tenant burst config: `STANDARD | SILVER | GOLD`.
- Implements weighted fairness in the admission controller using tier weights (default weights: STANDARD=1.0, SILVER=1.5, GOLD=2.0) but with hard constraints:
  - Anti-starvation floor: every enabled tenant gets a minimum refill share when contended (`min_refill_share_bps`, default 250 bps) so STANDARD tenants cannot be fully starved by higher tiers.
  - Max advantage clamp: effective weight ratio is capped (`max_weight_ratio`, default 2.5) to keep GOLD from dominating when there are few tenants.
  - Burst cap always wins: tiering does not bypass per-tenant burst caps, cooldown windows, or global fleet safety caps.
- Determinism: admission decisions remain deterministic for a (tenant, pool, request_size, timestamp_bucket) input. Tier weights and constraints are part of the evaluated policy snapshot; debug endpoint includes tier + derived weight/limits.
- Observability: adds labels for tier (low-cardinality) and exports per-tier admit/deny counts and computed “fair share” gauges for debugging.

Non-goals:
- No customer-configurable custom weights (fixed mapping for GA).
- No cross-region tier borrowing.

Rollout:
- Tier field is optional; defaults to STANDARD.
- Feature is guarded behind `burst.priority_tiers_enabled` policy flag (default off) and allow-listed per region/hardware class.

Testing:
- Unit tests for weight clamp + starvation floor.
- Integration tests for multi-tenant contention scenarios: ensures STANDARD still receives admits under sustained GOLD load.

Follow-ups:
- Add Console surface for tier (read-only) once customer UI work lands.
- Revisit defaults after beta telemetry (esp. min share bps vs tail latency).
commits: admission: add PriorityTier enum and config parsing/validation
fairness: implement tier-weighted refill with min share + max ratio clamp
policy: add burst.priority_tiers_enabled + defaults for min_refill_share_bps/max_weight_ratio
metrics: emit per-tier admit/deny + computed fair share
tests: add contention simulations + anti-starvation regression coverage
conversation: Keiko Yamamoto (review): Can we guarantee that a single GOLD tenant can’t pin the pool when there are many STANDARD tenants with small requests? I’m worried about starvation via request sizing + retries. Also, please document the exact constraints and defaults in an internal doc so SRE can reason about behavior.

Jordan Lee (author): Added two constraints: (1) min_refill_share_bps floor under contention and (2) max_weight_ratio clamp applied to derived weights. Also updated docs/internal/burst/priority_tiers.md with defaults, rationale, and examples. Request sizing is handled by the existing cost model (tokens->gpu_ms); the floor applies in cost space so small requests still accumulate admits for STANDARD.

Sean Gallagher (review): Metrics: please avoid adding tenant_id + tier together in the same metric series in the hot path; that can explode cardinality. Also, what’s the rollback plan if non-burst p95 regresses after enabling tiers?

Jordan Lee (author): Good catch—changed metrics to emit tier-only aggregates plus existing per-tenant series (without tier label) to avoid cross-product. For rollback: tiers are gated by burst.priority_tiers_enabled and region/hw allowlist; disabling flag reverts to current fairness behavior (weights=1.0 for all). This pairs with SLO gate PR (separate) that can auto-disable burst on regression.
Mina Haddad (review): Routing integration question: will denial reason codes change? We rely on stable reasons for fallback policy and customer messaging.

Jordan Lee (author): Denial reasons unchanged. Tiering only affects whether we can allocate from the pool; the denial code remains CAP_REACHED / FAIRNESS_LIMIT / POOL_SATURATED, etc. Debug endpoint now includes tier + computed effective weight to aid Support without changing client-visible codes.

Ethan Park (review): Please make sure the config migration is safe: if control plane hasn’t populated priority_tier yet, we should default to STANDARD and not reject the tenant model. Also add validation that only Dedicated tenants with burst enabled can set non-standard tiers (avoid accidental usage from other products).

Jordan Lee (author): Done. Proto field is optional; parsing defaults to STANDARD. Added validation in tenant_burst_config.ts: non-STANDARD tier requires dedicated_burst_enabled=true and enterprise_contract=true (control plane already sets this bit).

Vanessa Ortiz (review): Fleet perspective: I’m okay with weights, but I want the cap on advantage to be explicit. Can we keep max_weight_ratio configurable per pool class in policy (H100 vs L40S) so we can tune if supply is tight?
Jordan Lee (author): max_weight_ratio and min_refill_share_bps are policy parameters scoped by pool class (region/hw). Defaults included, can be tuned via policy without redeploy.
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add a short runbook note: if a STANDARD tenant complains about denials during a GOLD tenant burst, what do we check first?

Jordan Lee (author): Added a section in docs/internal/burst/priority_tiers.md: check pool saturation, per-tier admit/deny, effective weight clamp, and whether min_refill_share_bps is being applied (debug endpoint shows computed floor + last contention window).
Keiko Yamamoto (approval): Approved. The clamp + floor are the right guardrails. Let’s watch tail latency during beta and re-tune defaults if needed.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved with note: please ensure alert annotations mention when tiers are enabled so oncall has context.
release_notes: Dedicated burst: introduce optional priority tiers (STANDARD/SILVER/GOLD) for admission fairness under contention, with anti-starvation floor and capped advantage. Gated by policy flag and region/hardware allowlist.
